input: There are no competitors. My idea is a form for a student club to collect study-session availability. I observed our organizer chasing answers in a chat yesterday. Please check this possible alternative: https://workspace.google.com/products/forms/ . If you cannot access it, say so and request pasted material. What else might people do?
output:
**Established:** The idea is a form for your club to collect study-session availability, and it was prompted by observing an organizer chasing answers in a chat yesterday.
**Still unknown:** Whether you were the organizer or an observer, how big the club is, whether anyone already tried a scheduling tool in that chat, and how many people you could actually reach to test this.

Before the research — one thing worth naming: "there are no competitors" is a strong claim, and it turned out not to hold up once I looked. That's not a knock on the idea; group scheduling is a well-trodden problem, so the more useful question becomes *why would your club members switch from what they do now* rather than *does anything else exist*. What made you confident there was nothing out there already — had you searched, or was that more of an assumption going in?

Here's what I found, each recorded with source, access date, who it's for, what it offers, and the one narrow claim I'll actually stand behind:

| Source | Accessed | Target user | Offering | Narrow claim supported |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [workspace.google.com/products/forms](https://workspace.google.com/products/forms/) | 2026-09-07 | General individuals/orgs, not scheduling-specific | Generic form/survey builder; results export to Sheets | This is a general-purpose form tool that *could* be repurposed for availability collection, but has no built-in overlap/heatmap logic for scheduling. Vendor's own marketing page — treat as vendor claim, not neutral fact. |
| [doodle.com/en/group-poll-survey](https://doodle.com/en/group-poll-survey/) | 2026-09-07 | Teams/orgs coordinating group meetings | Purpose-built group-poll scheduler with proposed time slots, calendar sync, real-time responses, a free tier ("Try it free") | This is a scheduling-specific competitor, not just a substitute — vendor's own page, so the free-tier limits and "for any size group" framing are vendor claims, not independently verified. |
| [when2meet.com](https://www.when2meet.com/) | 2026-09-07 | Casual/informal groups | I directly loaded the live tool and saw a working drag-to-select calendar grid — confirms it's a functioning scheduling product today | I could **not** confirm pricing or account requirements directly from the page content itself (it rendered as a bare calendar with no about/pricing text) — so I'm not stating "free, no account required" as fact from this source. Third-party blog summaries claim that, but I haven't verified it on the primary site, so I'm flagging it as unverified rather than asserting it. |

So at minimum, Doodle is a direct, purpose-built competitor already solving group availability polling, and Google Forms/When2meet are viable substitutes. That contradicts "no competitors" — it doesn't kill your idea, but it does shift the useful question toward *why your club specifically isn't already using one of these*, which is exactly what Step 4 (reasons to switch) will need.

To get there, a few questions:

1. In that chat yesterday — were *you* the organizer chasing answers, or did you watch someone else do it? (Direct experience vs. observation changes how much weight that one data point carries.)
2. Did the organizer (or anyone in the chat) already try a poll tool like Doodle or a shared spreadsheet, or was it purely "everyone reply with your times"? That tells us what the real current workaround is.
3. Roughly how many people are in your club, and how many could you realistically message this week to ask about their last scheduling headache?
